title: On Waking
subtitle: The first words of the day — gratitude before the screen

chapters.heading: On Waking
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught the first words of consciousness: 'All praise is for Allah who gave us life after death, and to Him is the resurrection.' Sleep is the daily rehearsal for death; waking, its resurrection. Say it before the screen — let gratitude be the first thing the day touches.
chapters.dua: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
chapters.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
chapters.tl: Alḥamdu lillāhil-ladhī 'aḥyānā ba`da mā 'amātanā wa 'ilayhin-nushūr.

title: Before Sleep (1) — Ayat al-Kursi
subtitle: The devil himself taught it, and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed it was true

chapters.heading: Before Sleep (1) — Ayat al-Kursi
chapters.body: Abu Hurayrah caught a thief taking from the Ramadan zakat and let him go; the third time the thief offered to teach him words that Allah would benefit him by: when you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi to its end, and a guard from Allah will stay with you and no devil will come near you until morning. The Prophet ﷺ said that he had told the truth, though he is a liar, and that it was Shaytan (Bukhari 2311). Ayat al-Kursi is the Throne Verse, the great verse of Surat al-Baqarah on Allah's life, knowledge and sovereignty. One recitation at bedtime.
chapters.dua: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi before sleep, a guardian from Allah remains over him and no devil approaches him until morning.
chapters.arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٞ وَلَا نَوۡمٞۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءٖ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
chapters.tl: Allaahu laa 'ilaaha 'illaa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyoom. Laa ta'khudhuhu sinatunw-wa laa nawm. Lahu maa fis-samaawaati wa maa fil-'ard. Man dhal-ladhee yashfa'u 'indahoo 'illaa bi'idhnih. Ya'lamu maa bayna 'aydeehim wa maa khalfahum, wa laa yuheetoona bishay'im-min 'ilmihee 'illaa bimaa shaa'. Wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samaawaati wal-'ard, wa laa ya'ooduhoo hifzuhumaa, wa Huwal-'Aliyyul-'Azeem

title: Before Sleep (2) — The Three Quls
subtitle: The complete shield, wiped over the body

chapters.heading: Before Sleep (2) — The Three Quls
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ would recite the three quls, blow into his palms, and pass them over his face and what he could reach of his body — three times (Bukhari 5017). The complete shield: the purity of faith, the refuge from creation's harms, the refuge from the whisperers. Three small surahs the whole family can memorize in a week.
chapters.dua: Recite al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas; blow into the hands; wipe over whatever you can reach of the body.
chapters.arabic:
بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ لَمۡ يَلِدۡ وَلَمۡ يُولَدۡ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدُۢ
بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلۡفَلَقِ مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَٰتِ فِي ٱلۡعُقَدِ وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ مِن شَرِّ ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ ٱلَّذِي يُوَسۡوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
chapters.tl: Bismillaahir-Rahmaanir-Raheem. Qul huwal-laahu 'ahad Allaahus-samad Lam yalid wa lam yoolad Wa lam yakul-lahoo kufuwan 'ahad Bismillaahir-Rahmaanir-Raheem. Qul 'a'oozu birabbil-falaq Min sharri maa khalaq Wa min sharri ghaasiqin 'izaa waqab Wa min sharrin-naffaasaati fil-'uqad Wa min sharri haasidin 'izaa hasad Bismillaahir-Rahmaanir-Raheem. Qul 'a'oozu birabbin-naas Malikin-naas 'Ilaahin-naas Min sharril-waswaasil-khannaas Allazee yuwaswisu fee sudoorin-naas Minal-jinnati wan-naas

title: Entering the Home
subtitle: The threshold is a border — cross it with the Name
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 5096 (the wording of this dua — graded daʿif by al-Albani)

chapters.heading: Entering the Home
chapters.body: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, I ask You the good of entering and the good of leaving. In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we rely.' This wording is reported in Abu Dawud 5096, a narration scholars (al-Albani among them) grade daʿif, so treat the words as a customary dua, not a certain text. What is established is saying Bismillah on entering: then Shaytan tells his companion 'no lodging or supper here tonight' (Muslim 2018). The threshold is a border — cross it with the Name and the house changes citizenship.
chapters.dua: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ الْمَوْلَجِ وَخَيْرَ الْمَخْرَجِ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا، وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا، وَعَلَى رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا
chapters.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ الْمَوْلَجِ وَخَيْرَ الْمَخْرَجِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا

title: Before Eating
subtitle: Bismillah gathers the table

chapters.heading: Before Eating
chapters.body: Begin with Bismillah; if you forget at the start, say: 'Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirahu — in the name of Allah, its beginning and its end' (Abu Dawud 3767, sahih per al-Albani). The table is where the family gathers — let the Name gather it first.
chapters.dua: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَإِنْ نَسِيتَ: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ
chapters.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ نَسِيتَ فَقُلْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ

title: After Eating
subtitle: Praise for the morsel and the sip
sources: Sahih Muslim 2734 (praising Allah after a morsel and a sip)
Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3457 (daif per Darussalam); Sunan Abi Dawud 3850 (daif per al-Albani) (the wording of this dua — graded daʿif)

chapters.heading: After Eating
chapters.body: 'All praise is for Allah who fed us, gave us drink, and made us Muslims.' This exact wording is reported in Tirmidhi 3457 (daif per Darussalam) and Abu Dawud 3850 (daif per al-Albani), both graded daʿif; what is established is the praise itself — the Prophet ﷺ said Allah is pleased with the servant who says Alhamdulillah when taking a morsel of food or a drink (Muslim 2734).
chapters.dua: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
chapters.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ

title: The Journey
subtitle: The journey dua — from camels to planes
sources: Qur'an 43:13-14; Sahih Muslim 1342; Sunan Abi Dawud 2602 (sahih per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: The Journey
chapters.body: 'Allah is the Greatest' three times, then: 'Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have [otherwise] subdued it. And indeed we, to our Lord, will [surely] return' (Qur'an 43:13-14). Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet ﷺ did exactly this when he mounted his camel to set out on a journey (Muslim 1342). Ali reported the same dua in another order: Bismillah as the foot goes in the stirrup, Alhamdulillah when seated, then the dua, then Alhamdulillah three times, Allahu Akbar three times and a request for forgiveness (Abu Dawud 2602, sahih per al-Albani). Board the plane, start the car: the same dua carried camels and now carries engines.
chapters.dua: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ
chapters.tl: Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Subḥāna 'l-ladhi sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn. Wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn.

title: The Heart's Unrest
subtitle: The 3am dua for the racing heart

chapters.heading: The Heart's Unrest
chapters.body: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, incapacity and laziness, miserliness and cowardice, the burden of debt and being overpowered by men' (Bukhari 6369). The Prophet ﷺ used to ask for this refuge. Say it slowly — one breath per clause.
chapters.dua: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْبُخْلِ وَالْجُبْنِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ وَالْبُخْلِ وَالْجُبْنِ وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
chapters.tl: Allāhumma 'innī 'a`ūdhu bika mina 'l-ḥammi wa 'l-ḥuzn, wa 'l-`ajzi wa 'l-kasal, wa 'l-bukhli wa 'l-jubn, wa ḍala`id-dayn, wa ghalabatir-rijāl.

title: The Dua of Distress
subtitle: What the Prophet ﷺ used to say in distress

chapters.heading: The Dua of Distress
chapters.body: 'There is no deity but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no deity but Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne. There is no deity but Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Noble Throne.' Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to say this at a time of distress (Bukhari 6346). Say it as he did, and take the other means too: speak to someone you trust, and see a doctor or counsellor if the weight does not lift.
chapters.dua: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ
chapters.arabic: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ
chapters.tl: Lā ilāha illallāh al-`Aẓīmul-Ḥalīm, lā ilāha illallāh Rabbu 'l-`Arshi 'l-'Aẓīm, lā ilāha illallāh Rabbus-samāwāti wa Rabbu 'l-arḍ wa Rabbu 'l-`Arshi 'l-Karīm.

title: The Debtor's Dua
subtitle: Sufficiency from the only true sufficiency
sources: Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3563 (hasan per al-Albani and Darussalam)

chapters.heading: The Debtor's Dua
chapters.body: 'O Allah, suffice me with Your halal against Your haram, and enrich me by Your bounty from all besides You' (Tirmidhi 3563, hasan per al-Albani and Darussalam). Ali (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught it, and he passed it to a man who could not pay off his contract of freedom. For every wallet stretched thin by a buy-now age.
chapters.dua: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
chapters.tl: Allāhummak-finī biḥalālika `an ḥarāmik, wa 'aghninī bi faḍlika `amman siwāk.

title: For the Sick
subtitle: The Prophet's dua over a patient
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 5675; Sunan Abi Dawud 3106 (sahih per al-Albani); Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2083 (sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam)

chapters.heading: For the Sick
chapters.body: 'Remove the harm, O Lord of mankind; heal — You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness.' Aisha reported that the Prophet ﷺ made this dua when he visited a patient (Bukhari 5675). A different report has a dua said seven times over a sick person: 'I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to cure you' (Abu Dawud 3106, sahih per al-Albani; Tirmidhi 2083, sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam). Pair either with the doctor — tawakkul never cancelled the means.
chapters.dua: أَذْهِبِ الْبَاسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، اشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي، لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاوُكَ، شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
chapters.arabic: أَذْهِبِ الْبَاسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ اشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاوُكَ شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا

title: When Struck by Loss
subtitle: Umm Salama's dua — and what replaced her loss

chapters.heading: When Struck by Loss
chapters.body: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with better.' Umm Salama said it at her husband's death, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'if you do this, Allah will reward you and give you better' — and she was later married to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (Muslim 918). The loss is real; the return is real; the replacement is His specialty.
chapters.dua: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ، اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي وَاخْلُفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
chapters.arabic: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي وَاخْلُفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
chapters.tl: Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rāji`ūn, Allāhumma-jurni fī muṣībatī wa 'khluf lī khayran minhā.

title: Istikhara's Heart
subtitle: The dua of surrender for every decision

chapters.heading: Istikhara's Heart
chapters.body: 'O Allah, if You know this matter to be good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and my outcome — decree it for me, ease it for me, and bless me in it. And if You know it to be bad for me — turn it away from me, turn me away from it, and decree good for me wherever it is.' Pray two rak'ahs, say it, and then go ahead with the matter (Bukhari 6382). Reading ease or closed doors as the answer is the common understanding, not words of the hadith.
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ
chapters.tl: Allāhumma in kunta ta`lamu anna hādha 'l-amra khayrun lī fī dīnī wa ma`āshī wa `āqibati amrī, faqdurhu lī wa yassirhu lī thumma bārik lī fīh, wa in kunta ta`lamu anna hādha 'l-amra sharrun lī fī dīnī wa ma`āshī wa `āqibati 'amrī, faṣrifhu `annī waṣrifnī `anh, waqdur liya 'l-khayra ḥaythu kān,

title: For Parents
subtitle: The dua embedded in their right

chapters.heading: For Parents
chapters.body: 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small' (17:24). The dua embedded in the verse of their right. It is for living parents in their old age, and it is a dua a child can keep making for parents who have passed.
chapters.arabic: رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا

familyQuestion: Which person in your life needs this dua most this week — and will you tell them you prayed it?

title: For the Children
subtitle: The family dua — and a prayer for each child by name

chapters.heading: For the Children
chapters.body: 'Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous' (25:74). This is the dua of the servants of the Most Merciful, whom Surat al-Furqan describes. Pair it with praying for each child by name: the Prophet ﷺ prayed for Ibn Abbas that Allah make him learned in the religion (Bukhari 143).
chapters.dua: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
chapters.arabic: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا

title: Breaking the Fast
subtitle: The small door between two joys
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 2357 (hasan per al-Albani); Sahih al-Bukhari 1904; Sunan Ibn Majah 1753 (daif per al-Albani, hasan per Darussalam)

chapters.heading: Breaking the Fast
chapters.body: 'The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills' (Abu Dawud 2357, hasan per al-Albani). The Prophet ﷺ said: the fasting person has two joys — one at iftar, one at meeting his Lord (Bukhari 1904). Another report says the fasting person's dua at breaking the fast is not turned back (Ibn Majah 1753, daif per al-Albani, hasan per Darussalam). The dua is the small door between the two joys.
chapters.dua: ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَثَبَتَ الْأَجْرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
chapters.arabic: ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَثَبَتَ الْأَجْرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
chapters.tl: Dhahabaẓ-ẓama', wabtallati 'l-`urūq, wa thabata 'l-'ajru in shā Allāh.

familyQuestion: Which person in your life needs this dua most this week — and will you tell them you prayed it?

title: When It Rains
subtitle: Address the weather to its Owner

chapters.heading: When It Rains
chapters.body: 'O Allah, make it a beneficial downpour' (Bukhari 1032). And when the rain falls hard: 'O Allah, around us and not upon us' (Bukhari 1014). The weather, like everything else, is addressed to its Owner first.
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَيِّبًا نَافِعًا
chapters.tl: Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfi`a.

familyQuestion: Which person in your life needs this dua most this week — and will you tell them you prayed it?

title: Entering the Mosque
subtitle: Open the doors of mercy, then two rak'ahs
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 466 (sahih per al-Albani) (the refuge phrase); Sunan Ibn Majah 771 (daif per Darussalam) (Bismillah, was-salamu ʿala Rasulillah); Sahih Muslim 713 (open for me the doors of Your mercy); Sahih al-Bukhari 444 (two rak'ahs before sitting)

chapters.heading: Entering the Mosque
chapters.body: 'I seek refuge in Allah the Magnificent, in His noble countenance and His eternal authority, from the accursed devil. In the name of Allah; peace and blessings upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' Then two rak'ahs of greeting before sitting (Bukhari 444).
chapters.dua: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَبِوَجْهِهِ الْكَرِيمِ وَسُلْطَانِهِ الْقَدِيمِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
chapters.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَبِوَجْهِهِ الْكَرِيمِ وَسُلْطَانِهِ الْقَدِيمِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
chapters.tl: 'A`ūdhu billāhi l-`aẓīm, wa bi-wajhihil-karīm, wa sultānihil-qadīm, min ash-shaytānir-rajīm. Bismillāhi, wassalātu wassalāmu `alā rasūlillāhi. Allāhummaftaḥ lī 'abwāba raḥmatik.

familyQuestion: Which person in your life needs this dua most this week — and will you tell them you prayed it?

title: After the Prayer
subtitle: Say it after every obligatory prayer, before the dhikr

chapters.heading: After the Prayer
chapters.body: I seek Allah's forgiveness (3x). O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, O Owner of Majesty and Honor.
chapters.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ تَبَارَكْتَ يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
chapters.tl: Astaghfirullāh, Astaghfirullāh, Astaghfirullāh. Allāhumma antas-salām, wa minkas-salām, tabārakta yā dhal-Jalāli wal-'Ikrām.
chapters.tlSource: Hisn 66 (sunnah.com/hisn:66); the three repetitions are written out

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: Sayyid al-Istighfar — the Master of Seeking Forgiveness
subtitle: Whoever says it with conviction morning or evening and dies that day/night enters Paradise

chapters.heading: Sayyid al-Istighfar — the Master of Seeking Forgiveness
chapters.body: O Allah, You are my Lord, none has the right to be worshipped but You. You created me and I am Your servant... (complete form in Sahih al-Bukhari 6306)
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَىٰ عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
chapters.tl: Allāhumma anta Rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa anā `abduk, wa anā `alā `ahdika wa wa`dika mastaṭa`t, a`ūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣana`t, abū'u laka bi ni`matika `alay, wa abū'u laka bidhanbī faghfir lī fa'innahu lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant.
chapters.tlSource: Hisn 79 (sunnah.com/hisn:79); 'laka' added before 'bidhanbī' to follow Sahih al-Bukhari 6306 (sunnah.com/bukhari:6306)

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: The Sum of all Duas
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ most frequent supplication (Bukhari, number not re-checked)

chapters.heading: The Sum of all Duas
chapters.body: Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
chapters.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
chapters.tl: Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā ḥasanah wa fi 'l-ākhirati ḥasanah wa qinā `adhāban-nār.

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: Leaving for Work or Study
subtitle: Said when leaving the house — the caller says: you are guided, sufficed, and protected

chapters.heading: Leaving for Work or Study
chapters.body: In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah.
chapters.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
chapters.tl: Bismillāhi, tawakkaltu `alallāhi, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: Asking for Rain
subtitle: Raise the hands and ask — the Prophet ﷺ did

chapters.heading: Asking for Rain
chapters.body: O Allah, send us rain (3x). Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ raised both hands and said this when asked for rain (Bukhari 1014); at the prayer for rain he also wore his cloak inside out (Bukhari 1012).
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا، اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا، اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا
chapters.tl: Allāhumma aghithnā, Allāhumma aghithnā, Allāhumma aghithnā.

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: After Fajr: Knowledge, Provision, Deeds
subtitle: What the Prophet ﷺ used to say after the morning prayer
sources: Sunan Ibn Majah 925 (daif per Darussalam; sahih per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: After Fajr: Knowledge, Provision, Deeds
chapters.body: 'O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, goodly provision and acceptable deeds.' Umm Salamah reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to say this when he gave the salam of the morning prayer (Ibn Majah 925, daif per Darussalam; sahih per al-Albani, so hold it as a customary dua). Provision here sits between knowledge and deeds: ask for what is good, not only for more.
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلاً مُتَقَبَّلاً
chapters.dua: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلاً مُتَقَبَّلاً
chapters.tl: Allāhumma innī as'aluka `ilman nāfi`an, wa rizqan ṭayyiban, wa `amalan mutaqabbalan.
chapters.tlSource: Transliteration after the fawazahmed0/hadith-api English edition of the Ibn Majah report; diacritics added by the app

title: The Hawqala — the Treasure of Paradise
subtitle: A treasure of Paradise — said when matters weigh heavy

chapters.heading: The Hawqala — the Treasure of Paradise
chapters.body: There is no might nor power except with Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says it has uttered a treasure of Paradise (Sahih al-Bukhari 6384), and it is reported in Muslim 2704 as well. Say it when a matter feels larger than your strength.
chapters.arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
chapters.tl: Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata 'illā billāh.

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: Seeing Someone Afflicted
subtitle: Say it quietly — and never say it as pride, only gratitude
sources: Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3431 (daif per Darussalam; hasan per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: Seeing Someone Afflicted
chapters.body: Praise is to Allah who spared me what He has afflicted you with, and favored me over much of His creation. Tirmidhi 3431 reports it; its graders differ (daif per Darussalam, hasan per al-Albani), so hold it as a customary dua. Say it quietly, and never over the person themselves.
chapters.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي عَافَانِي مِمَّا ابْتَلَاكَ بِهِ وَفَضَّلَنِي عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ تَفْضِيلًا
chapters.tl: Alhamdu lillāhi 'l-ladhī `āfānī mimmab-talāka bihi wa faḍḍalanī `alā kathīrin mimman khalaqa tafḍīlā.

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: The Night Prayer's Door
subtitle: Aisha asked what to say if she knew Laylat al-Qadr — this was the answer
sources: Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3513 (daif per Darussalam; sahih per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: The Night Prayer's Door
chapters.body: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon — pardon me. Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ what to say if she knew which night was Laylat al-Qadr, and this was his answer (Tirmidhi 3513, daif per Darussalam; sahih per al-Albani). The night is worth more than a thousand months (97:3) — and its door fits inside one breath. Say it through the last odd nights, hopefully, without counting.
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي

familyQuestion: Who in your family needs this dua tonight — and will you tell them you prayed it for them?

title: Istikhara — Asking Allah to Choose
subtitle: Two rak'ahs, then this dua, naming the matter in your heart — then proceed with what unfolds

chapters.heading: Istikhara — Asking Allah to Choose
chapters.body: O Allah, if You know this matter to be good for my religion, my livelihood, and the end of my affair, decree it for me, make it easy, and bless it. And if You know it to be bad, turn it away from me and turn me from it — then decree good for me wherever it lies and content me with it.
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ
chapters.tl: Allāhumma innī astakhīruka bi `ilmik, wa astaqdiruka biqudratik, wa as'aluka min faḍlika 'l-`Aẓīm, fa'innaka taqdiru wa lā aqdir, wa ta`lamu wa lā a`lam, wa anta `allāmu 'l-ghuyūb, Allāhumma in kunta ta`lamu anna hādha 'l-amra khayrun lī fī dīnī wa ma`āshī wa `āqibati amrī, faqdurhu lī wa yassirhu lī thumma bārik lī fīh, wa in kunta ta`lamu anna hādha 'l-amra sharrun lī fī dīnī wa ma`āshī wa `āqibati 'amrī, faṣrifhu `annī waṣrifnī `anh, waqdur liya 'l-khayra ḥaythu kān, thumma arḍinī bih.

title: At Suhoor — the Fast Begins
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ said: actions are by intentions — the fast is born at suhoor
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1 (actions are by intentions) — the spoken wording is customary, not a reported text

chapters.heading: At Suhoor — the Fast Begins
chapters.body: I intend the fast of tomorrow from the month of Ramadan (the intention is in the heart; saying these words is customary, not a reported wording).
chapters.arabic: وَبِصَوْمِ غَدٍ نَّوَيْتُ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ

title: The Full Journey Dua
subtitle: Say the takbir three times when boarding; this when setting out

chapters.heading: The Full Journey Dua
chapters.body: Glory to Him who subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey for righteousness and taqwa, and deeds You are pleased with.
chapters.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَىٰ
chapters.tl: Subḥāna 'l-ladhi sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn. Wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn. Allāhumma innā nas'aluka fī safarinā hādha 'l-birra wat-taqwā, Wa mina 'l-`amali mā tarḍā,

familyQuestion: Which person in your family needs this dua most this week — and will you teach it to them?

title: Inside the Prostration
subtitle: Then pour out your own words — the slave is nearest to his Lord in sujud (Muslim 482)

chapters.heading: Inside the Prostration
chapters.body: Glory to my Lord, the Most High (three times in prostration — Sahih Muslim 772). Then pour out your own words, for the slave is nearest to his Lord while prostrating (Sahih Muslim 482). The posture says what the tongue cannot: the forehead on the earth, the heart at the Throne.
chapters.arabic: سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَىٰ
chapters.tl: Subḥāna Rabbiya 'l-a`lā.

familyQuestion: Which person in your family needs this dua most this week — and will you teach it to them?

title: Between the Two Prostrations
subtitle: The sitting between sujud is built for asking
sources: Sunan Ibn Majah 897 (sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam)

chapters.heading: Between the Two Prostrations
chapters.body: My Lord, forgive me — my Lord, forgive me (said between the two prostrations, Ibn Majah 897, sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam). The sitting between sujud is built for asking: the body rests a breath, and the heart rises. The dua is deliberately short, so every tongue, new or old, can carry it.
chapters.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي
chapters.tl: Rabbi'ghfir lī, Rabbi'ghfir lī.

familyQuestion: Which person in your family needs this dua most this week — and will you teach it to them?

title: The Witr Qunut
subtitle: Taught to al-Hasan ibn Ali by the Prophet ﷺ
sources: Sunan an-Nasa'i 1745 (sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam)

chapters.heading: The Witr Qunut
chapters.body: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, pardon me among those You have pardoned, turn to me in friendship among those on whom You have turned in friendship, bless what You have given, and save me from the evil of what You have decreed, for You decree and none decrees against You. Al-Hasan ibn Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught him these words for the qunut of witr (Nasa'i 1745, sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam).
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي فِيمَنْ هَدَيْتَ، وَعَافِنِي فِيمَنْ عَافَيْتَ، وَتَوَلَّنِي فِيمَنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ، وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، وَقِنِي شَرَّ مَا قَضَيْتَ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْضِي وَلَا يُقْضَى عَلَيْكَ، إِنَّهُ لَا يَذِلُّ مَنْ وَالَيْتَ، تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ

familyQuestion: Which person in your family needs this dua most this week — and will you teach it to them?

title: Visiting the Sick
subtitle: What the Prophet ﷺ used to say when he visited the sick

chapters.heading: Visiting the Sick
chapters.body: No harm — a purification, if Allah wills (la ba's, tuhur in sha Allah — Sahih al-Bukhari 3616). Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to say this when he visited the sick. The sick bedouin answered that it was a fever that would lead him to the grave, and the Prophet ﷺ said: then so be it. The words do not deny the illness — they dress it with meaning: this suffering, carried with sabr, washes rather than stains. Then sit a while; presence itself is half the medicine. (A separate dua said seven times over the sick person is under For the Sick.)
chapters.arabic: لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
chapters.tl: Lā ba'sa ṭahūrun in shā Allāh.

title: The Morning Shield (Complete)
subtitle: Whenever you stop at a place, and in the evening (Muslim 2708, 2709)

chapters.heading: The Morning Shield (Complete)
chapters.body: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created. Khawla bint Hakim reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever stops at a place and says this will not be harmed until he moves on (Muslim 2708). A man stung by a scorpion in the night was told that had he said it in the evening it would not have harmed him (Muslim 2709).
chapters.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
chapters.tl: A`ūdhu bikalimāti-llāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.

title: The Evening Shield
subtitle: Said as the body settles — the night given back to its Owner

chapters.heading: The Evening Shield
chapters.body: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live (Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya — Sahih al-Bukhari 6324). Hudhayfah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said it when he went to bed. Said as the body settles into the night it was given back to its Owner. Pair it with Ayat al-Kursi: Abu Hurayrah was told that no devil will come near the one who recites it at bedtime until morning, and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed it (Bukhari 2311). Say the words, and even sleep becomes worship.
chapters.arabic: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا
chapters.tl: Bismika Allāhumma amūtu wa aḥyā.

title: Over Your Children
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge with these words for al-Hasan and al-Husayn

chapters.heading: Over Your Children
chapters.body: I seek protection for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and poisonous creature, and from every evil eye. Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge for al-Hasan and al-Husayn with these words, saying that Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ismail and Ishaq with them (Bukhari 3371).
chapters.arabic: أُعِيذُكُمَا بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
chapters.tl: U`īthukumā bikalimāti 'llāhit-tāmmati min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli `aynin lāmmah

title: The Ten Days' Takbir
subtitle: The loud glorification of Dhul-Hijjah's first ten days
sources: Practice of the scholars (wording not traced to a numbered hadith); Qur'an 89:2

chapters.heading: The Ten Days' Takbir
chapters.body: Allah is Greatest, Allah is Greatest; there is no god but Allah; Allah is Greatest, Allah is Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. Raising the takbir in the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah is a practice of the scholars; this wording has no hadith source in this app. Most commentators understand the 'ten nights' that Allah swears by (89:2) to be these days.
chapters.arabic: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ
